summary.text: The teacher analyzes karma-yoga through body, mind, discriminative intellect and senses, all used without possessiveness for purification. Atma-shuddhi means clearing the conditioned instrument, not cleaning the ever-pure self; a dusty mirror illustrates the distinction. This preparation leads toward knowledge rather than directly producing liberation. The next verse contrasts relinquished fruit-attachment and stable peace with desire-driven action and bondage. The same instruments can serve either orientation, and an unintegrated person need not be malicious. Questions distinguish the knower's non-identification from the seeker's practice, then use an actor maintaining inward identity while performing a role to explain inner renunciation and outer participation.

segments.heading: The lotus recap rejects separation from the ground

blocks.text: Dedication includes releasing the result while remaining within ordinary life. Sensory encounters are understood as appearances in consciousness rather than privately owned activities.
The teacher extends the lotus example to dependence on water: the individual is not an entity outside Brahman merely avoiding contact with it.

segments.heading: Four instruments share one non-possessive orientation

blocks.text: The preceding activity-list is grouped into body, mind, intellect and senses. Their common condition is relinquished attachment, and their stated purpose is purification.

Intellect is distinguished as determinative discrimination; sensory instruments are treated without an ego's possessiveness. Intellectual activity alone is not automatically karma-yoga without the purifying orientation.

segments.heading: Atma-shuddhi cleans the mirror, not the light

blocks.text: These yogis are practitioners, neither fully established knowers nor simply reward-seeking worshippers. Purification concerns the inner adjunct and its distortions, not an impurity intrinsic to Atma.
Cleaning a mirror allows unchanged light to appear clearly. The teacher explicitly places purification before knowledge and denies that action itself directly supplies liberation.
The commentary excludes possessiveness across all instruments, including the purpose of action. Arjuna is directed toward the practice fitting his present eligibility.

segments.heading: Relinquishing fruit-attachment leads toward stable peace

blocks.text: The contrast pairs integrated and unintegrated agents, relinquishment and clinging, peace and bondage. Peace is unfolded through psychological stillness toward knowledge-established fulfillment.
The teacher returns to sequential preparation and recognition. Sense-object interactions belong to nature; inward appropriation is not what makes them function.

segments.heading: Desire-driven action binds even a competent person

blocks.text: An unintegrated person need not be immoral. Desire for an owned result can govern competent and outwardly virtuous activity, keeping the sense of a separate claimant alive.
The familiar attachment-to-anger sequence explains renewed bondage. The commentary contrasts this with purification, knowledge, renunciation and establishment; the next verse is only previewed.

segments.heading: The knower and practitioner integrate differently

blocks.text: Asked how integration works with an individual body, the teacher distinguishes an observer's prarabdha-description from the knower's non-agency. Dream witnessing illustrates non-identification.

The practitioner understands the teaching but still seeks its firm recognition. Relinquishing fruit-attachment loosens the individuality that survives intellectual understanding; a participant's distinction between purification terms receives brief assent.

segments.heading: The actor illustrates inner abidance and outer participation

blocks.text: A participant asks for a fresh account of inner renunciation and outer participation. The teacher compares someone playing Julius Caesar while retaining the inward identity of the actor.
The role's required actions can be executed without making its events the actor's ultimate identity. The analogy points to inward self-abidance during bodily life, not avoidance of the role.
there is an inner abundance and external actions

concepts.label: buddhi
concepts.gloss: Determinative discrimination distinguished from ordinary mental activity.

concepts.label: Atma shuddhi
concepts.gloss: Purification of the conditioned inner instrument, not the ever-pure self.

concepts.label: Karma Yoga
concepts.gloss: Action oriented to purification rather than production of liberation.

concepts.label: Shanti
concepts.gloss: Peace unfolded from settled inwardness toward establishment in Brahman.

concepts.label: Sakshi
concepts.gloss: Witness standpoint used to explain the knower's non-identification.
